also: be on trial for one’s life

terms.comment: To bring someone to trial, in jūdicium addūcere; to be on trial for something, jūdicium dē aliquā rē subīre (Traupman 197); to stand trial, defending oneself, causam dīcere.

terms.gloss: a criminal trial; the standing court that tried one kind of crime
evidence: Cic. Fin. 2.54: cum praetor quaestiōnem inter sīcāriōs exercuisset (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Held before a praetor and a jury; to conduct a trial, quaestiōnem exercēre (Traupman 197).
Classically a judicial examination before a magistrate. To hold a hearing, cognitiōnem habēre (Traupman).

phrases.latin: omnia jūdicia aut distrahendārum contrōversiārum aut pūniendōrum maleficiōrum causā reperta sunt
phrases.english: all trials were devised either to settle disputes or to punish crimes
A famous trial was being held.

phrases.source: Traupman 197; cf. Cic. Fin. 2.54: quaestiōnem inter sīcāriōs (Lewis & Short s.v. exerceō)

phrases.english: to be on trial for one’s life
to go to court, go on trial
phrases.source: Traupman 197; cf. Nep. Att. 6.4 (Lewis & Short s.v. jūs)
